column1: # clues.tsv for ft_memcpy -- pedagogic hints only, each a question. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><CASE label><TAB>...   (a hint fires when ANY of its cases fails)
man memcpy: it "copies n bytes from memory area src to memory area dest". How many bytes does your function copy, from where to where, and what does it do when n is 0?
What does memcpy return (man memcpy, RETURN VALUE) -- and is that the pointer your function hands back on every path?
memcpy copies bytes of memory, not a string: what decides when your function stops -- n, or something it finds in src? And what does it do with a byte of 0x80 or more?
If the small rows pass and this one does not, does anything in your function depend on n being small, or on what the bytes hold? This source holds NULs and bytes of 0x80 or more.
